entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Valerius Maximus was a 1st-century Latin writer and author of a collection of historical anecdotes: Factorum et dictorum memorabilium libri IX. He worked during the reign of Tiberius, producing a work that would serve as a valuable source of information for later historians, including the Roman historian Suetonius.

Maximus' writing was characterized by its focus on the lives and deeds of notable individuals, often with a moral or instructive purpose. His work was widely studied and admired in the Roman Empire, and it remains an important source of information on the history of the period.

Despite his significance as a historical source, Maximus himself is relatively little known outside of scholarly circles. His life and work are the subject of ongoing research and debate among historians, who continue to study and interpret his writings in the context of the broader Roman Empire.

For the modern reader, Maximus' work offers a fascinating glimpse into the cultural and intellectual values of the Roman Empire, as well as the ways in which historical memory and tradition were constructed and transmitted during this period.
